2610.07128.title: Aggregating User Preferences while Ensuring Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion using Graph Summarization
2610.07128.paper_summary: Aggregating the preferences of diverse user groups into a collective outcome raises fundamental challenges of equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI): classical aggregation rules such as Borda and Condorcet have no mechanism to prevent results from systematically favoring majority groups, collapsing onto homogeneous items, or under-representing minorities. We address this problem through EDI-constrained graph summarization. User preferences are modeled as a weighted attributed bipartite graph, and a greedy coarsening algorithm iteratively merges user nodes while enforcing three structural EDI criteria: an equity gap constraint ($ΔE$), an intra-list diversity constraint (ILD), and a group inclusion constraint. Rather than correcting fairness after aggregation, our method embeds EDI preservation directly into the graph structure. We evaluate across five datasets spanning four domains: MovieLens 100k and 1M, libimseti.cz, Rate My Professors, and OpenAlex (2018-2023). Our method, AURORA, achieves the largest and most consistent diversity gains over classical voting rules, and on MovieLens 100k at $k = 20$ it simultaneously improves all three EDI criteria over both Borda and Condorcet. On Rate My Professors, it combines high diversity (ILD = 0.808) with the highest female item representation (60%), at a moderate equity cost, and it achieves the lowest equity gap ($ΔE = 0.031$) on OpenAlex, where Borda-based methods recommend zero female authors. On libimseti.cz, the only dataset where the sensitive attribute is present on both sides of the bipartite graph, our method does not reduce the equity gap, a limitation we connect to prior findings that demographic parity is not always an appropriate target. These results demonstrate that embedding EDI constraints into aggregation structure yields more robust fairness-diversity trade-offs than post-hoc approaches.
2610.07128.paper_summary_zh: 聚合多元用戶群的偏好以達成集體結果，提出了公平性、多樣性和包容性（EDI）的基本挑戰：傳統的聚合規則如博達和孔多塞並沒有機制來防止結果系統性地偏向多數群體、陷入同質化項目或低估少數群體。我們通過受EDI約束的圖形摘要來解決這個問題。用戶偏好被建模為加權屬性雙部圖，並且一個貪婪的粗化算法在強制執行三個結構性EDI標準的同時，迭代地合併用戶節點：公平差距約束（$ΔE$）、列表內部多樣性約束（ILD）和群體包容性約束。我們的方法不是在聚合後修正公平性，而是將EDI保護直接嵌入圖結構中。我們在涵蓋四個領域的五個數據集上進行評估：MovieLens 100k 和 1M、libimseti.cz、Rate My Professors 和 OpenAlex（2018-2023）。我們的方法AURORA在古典投票規則上實現了最大的和最一致的多樣性增益，在MovieLens 100k中，當$k = 20$時，它同時改善了所有三個EDI標準，相較於博達和孔多塞。在Rate My Professors上，它結合了高多樣性（ILD = 0.808）和最高的女性項目代表性（60%），在適度的公平成本下，並且在OpenAlex上實現了最低的公平差距（$ΔE = 0.031$），而基於博達的方法推薦零位女性作者。在libimseti.cz上，唯一一個敏感屬性在雙部圖的兩側都存在的數據集，我們的方法並未減少公平差距，這一限制我們與之前的發現聯繫起來，即人口平等並不總是適當的目標。這些結果表明，將EDI約束嵌入聚合結構中，產生的公平性-多樣性權衡比事後方法更為穩健。
